hints.title: Full Window Rescan Bottleneck Obstacle
hints.text: Scanning every k-length window independently takes O(N * k) time. How can maintaining an ordered double-ended structure of promising candidate indices allow finding the maximum in amortized O(1) per step?

hints.title: Monotonic Decreasing Window Invariant
hints.text: If index i < j and nums[i] <= nums[j], nums[i] can never be the maximum in any future window containing j. Maintaining strictly decreasing values keeps the maximum always at the front.

hints.title: Double-Ended Monotonic Window Procedure
hints.text: Maintain a double-ended list of indices. For each index i: remove indices from the front that are <= i - k. Pop indices from the back while their values are <= nums[i]. Append i to the back. When i >= k - 1, append the value at the front index to the result.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: N: length of array nums (1 <= N <= 10^5)
k: sliding window size (1 <= k <= N)
complexity.notes: Each index is pushed and popped from the double-ended queue at most once.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Scanning each of the N - k + 1 windows takes O(N * k) time, timing out for N = 10^5 and k = 10^4.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Maintaining at most k candidate indices in a monotonic double-ended queue bounds auxiliary space to O(k).
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Knowing why inferior older elements can be purged and amortizing operations to O(1) per element.
